summary: A fire lookout once stood on the summit of Slate Mountain near Flagstaff. It has been dismantled, the road is reclaimed, and only a hiking trail reaches the top.

facts.status_note: Lookout tower dismantled and removed; the service road was reclaimed by the forest and only a trail remains to the summit

access.note: Signed trailhead and parking on Forest Road 191, about two miles off US 180. Sources disagree on whether a low-clearance vehicle can manage the road.

visit.trail_note: 2.2-mile trail from a trailhead at 7,362 feet, following an old jeep road up an 853-foot climb to the summit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: westlookouts gives Slate Mountain as Navaho County under Apache-Sitgreaves NF, township 9N-23E-30, and gives the same township line for Springer Mountain. The FFLA list and the record say Coconino, and the hiking accounts place the peak near Flagstaff. The record's Coconino is kept.

SummitPost says the road is passable to low-clearance vehicles in all but the worst conditions. Arizona Hiking found it rocky and recommends high clearance. Not resolved; both are reported in the story.

notes_for_editor: No construction date, staffing history or removal date for the Slate Mountain lookout was found in any source read, so none is stated. The 'ground' type comes from the FFLA list. Do not confuse with the California Slate Mountain lookout site listed on firetower.org; that is a different lookout and was not used. Sources disagree on the forest road clearance (SummitPost low-clearance OK vs Arizona Hiking high clearance advised) and on the trailhead distance (2 miles vs 1.9 miles on FR 191). The westlookouts Navaho County entry looks like a copy error from the Springer Mountain line on the same page; the record's Coconino county and coordinates are kept. The 2.2-mile trail distance and 853-foot climb come from SummitPost.
